key_insight: The paper shows that neuromorphic AI can be made much more efficient by co-designing the network and the hardware together. A dual-memory spiking neural network mapped to a custom chip achieves over 4× higher throughput, 5× better energy efficiency, and 40–60% fewer parameters than prior methods.
problem_solved: Neuromorphic systems often face a mismatch between model design and hardware constraints, which limits speed, energy efficiency, and parameter efficiency. This work addresses how to build spiking networks that are both accurate and naturally suited to custom neuromorphic hardware.
method: Designed a spiking neural network with two memory pathways to better capture temporal information.
Co-optimized the model architecture with a custom neuromorphic chip for efficient execution.
Reduced parameter count while improving hardware utilization, enabling faster and lower-energy inference.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates that algorithm–hardware co-design can unlock major efficiency gains beyond software-only optimization. It is especially relevant for edge AI and always-on systems where power, latency, and model size matter.

paper_title: Algorithm–hardware co-design of neuromorphic networks with dual memory pathways
